current_events: A Board of Peace envoy meets Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu and urges a halt in strikes across the Gaza Strip. However, they also announce that Israel will not withdraw from the enclave until Hamas completely disarms
The United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs reports that dozens of children and civilians have been killed in weekend attacks in Gaza
Two Palestinians are reported to have been killed in an Israeli missile strike near a mosque at a civilian vehicle southwest of Gaza City

The Israel Defense Forces says that they have killed two Hamas militants in separate airstrikes in central Gaza and the Shati camp in Gaza City respectively, including a Nukhba Force commander who took part in the October 7 attacks
Shipping data shows that two tanker ships carrying oil from Saudi Arabia, the Suezmax Malta-flagged Lesvos and the VLCC Desh Vaibhav, have exited the Red Sea through the Bab-el-Mandeb strait
At least seven people are killed, including three children, and 40 others are injured in a Ukrainian drone strike on a crowded beach in Gelendzhik, Krasnodar Krai, Russia
The death toll from the two earthquakes that hit Venezuela in June exceeds past 6,000 according to figures from lawmaker Jorge Rodríguez
At least fourteen people are killed in a series of floods in southern India
Scotland's NatureScot denies a 2026 licence for hunting northern gannets (known locally as "gugas") on Sula Sgeir, citing possible harm to the local gannet population after recent bird-flu deaths
Italy experiences its fourth heatwave of the summer with the health ministry issuing red alerts for a record 25 cities
Michigan, U.S., reports the first two deaths of the current cyclosporiasis outbreak, which is caused by cyclospora cayetanensis
Poland's health ministry appeals a Brussels court ruling ordering the country to accept and pay approximately €1.3 billion for unwanted COVID-19 vaccine doses produced by Pfizer and BioNTech

Russian opposition politician Boris Nadezhdin, who attempted to contest the 2024 presidential election on a platform against the Russo-Ukrainian war, announces that he has fled the country to France following growing pressure on him and his family
In tennis, Alexandra Eala becomes the first Filipino player to win a WTA Tour title after defeating Jessica Pegula 4–6, 6–4, 6–0 to win the women's singles title at the 2026 Washington DC Open

In horse racing, Churchill Downs Incorporated and the New York Racing Association announce a new championship series for 3-year old Thoroughbreds beginning in 2027, involving the Kentucky Derby and Belmont Stakes, but notably omitting the traditional middle leg of the U.S. Triple Crown, the Preakness Stakes

Major League Soccer, the top flight of men's soccer in the U.S. and Canada, announces that Larry Berg, currently a co-owner of Los Angeles FC (LAFC) in that league, will succeed Don Garber as league commissioner at the start of 2027. Berg will sell his interest in LAFC before assuming his new position
